synopsis: Game engines provide reusable real-time visual worlds, making virtual job sites affordable and fast enough for the program’s four-month window, but machine and sensor models must be added separately [f13172, f13181]. Reported Unreal Engine 5 terrain-rendering results range from 60 FPS for a single building to 17 FPS for a 23-million-Gaussian scene, so demonstrated performance depends on scene scale [f3893, f3894]. CARLA 0.10.0 moved to Unreal Engine 5.5 with Chaos physics on 19 December 2024 and includes a mining earth-mover asset; the separate UE4 release 0.9.16 followed on 16 September 2025, making a frozen, qualified build advisable [f8464, f8297, f8466, f15938]. CARLA’s UE5 hardware requirements include an RTX 3000-series GPU or better, at least 16 GB VRAM and 130 GB disk space [f8850]. Visual realism is not validated sensor or braking physics: specialized machine behavior requires coupled physics tools, wavelength-specific sensor materials are absent from ordinary visual textures, and a 2026 study found photometric divergence in Unity construction scenes despite extensive domain randomization [f13178, f13179, f13182, f10584].
